newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria court rules PAI Bank insolvent.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria court rules PAI Bank insolvent.

text.p: The Sofia City Court on Tuesday declared the Private Agricultural and Investment Bank (PAIB) insolvent at the request of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), a court official said.
"The court ruled the bank insolvent from May 17, 1996 and appointed a liquidator," a court official told reporters.
In March 1996 the BNB cancelled PAIB's licence, citing its negative capital to risk assets ratio, illiquidity, balance losses and systematic violations of banking regulations.

The bank had a 795 million lev loss as of January 31, 1996. It suffered a severe liqudity shortage and was unable to meet outstanding payments of 250 million levs and to provision its risks assets, the BNB said.
The BNB sought PAIB's insolvency in June last year.
PAIB is the third bank declared insolvent by the court among the 16 local private and state banks against which the BNB has launched bankruptcy proceedings since May last year.
The other two banks ruled insolvent so far are the private Crystalbank and state-owned Mineralbank.
